paragraphs: Fonroche Lighting America designs and sells off-grid solar lighting for streets and roadways, parking lots, parks, pathways, campuses and other public infrastructure. The range runs from SmartLight solar streetlights to NOWATT solar bollards and solar studs.

Because each system operates independently of the grid, a project can skip underground cabling and utility connections. Pre-wired modular power centers hold the energy storage. The company says a crew can install and activate a lighting system in under an hour. Designs begin with an analysis of ten years of local solar data using the PVsyst software suite and Meteonorm historical irradiation data. Once installed, the lights can be monitored remotely through a wireless network called Fonroche Connect.

The systems are built for municipalities, tribal communities, federal campuses, developers and commercial properties. Case studies describe Augusta, Georgia, which addressed safety and budget problems on Windsor Spring Road by deploying 42 autonomous solar streetlights. In Rowlett, Texas, the city is installing 425 solar-powered SmartLights across a 5.5-mile stretch of three corridors. The American business took its present form when Fonroche Lighting acquired SolarOne Solutions and incorporated Fonroche Lighting America. The site invites visitors to join 1,000+ communities and businesses already using its lighting.

quote.text: Because reliability isn’t optional when you’re off the grid.
